03Structural systems

WHEN REPAIR HASTO BE ENGINEERED.

Prime Projects International provides specialised structural repair and strengthening solutions to restore, protect and enhance the integrity of damaged or aging structures.

Repair is planned around the cause of deterioration, not the surface symptom. Where capacity is affected, strengthening is coordinated with the structural requirement and the temporary works needed to execute it safely.

Scope typically includes

  • Concrete repair and reinstatement
  • Crack injection and corrosion treatment
  • Structural rehabilitation
  • Carbon fibre reinforcement
  • Engineered strengthening systems

How tagging is done (detailed, for DB migration)

  1. Normalize items: List each service/material as one record with a stable id and name (dummy IDs used now; DB will generate/assign real IDs).
  2. Assign primary category: Set one main tag per item — Construction, Finishing, Waterproofing, or Materials Trading — so items appear in the right section alongside existing ones.
  3. Add secondary tags: Attach multiple tags for cross-listing (e.g. waterproofing can also carry Finishing; trading items carry material tags like cement/paint). Store as a tag list/array or a join table.
  4. Set activity type: Mark each record as Service, Trading, or Both to separate execution work from buying/selling of materials.
  5. Persist to database (next step): Create tables such as items(id,name,primary_category,activity_type,...), tags(id,name), item_tags(item_id,tag_id). Seed with these dummy rows, then swap this static block to render from DB queries/API.
  6. Review: Deduplicate names, keep tag spelling consistent, and ensure every item has a primary category and activity type.

09HSE & quality

SAFETY IS OURFOUNDATION.QUALITY IS OURPROMISE.

Safe methods and verifiable quality are treated as part of the work itself — planned before mobilisation and checked as the work progresses.

Our HSE & quality approach

Method / Supervision / Verification

HSE

  • Health & Safety

    01

    Safe working methods, continuous monitoring and training are built into every project. Hazards are identified before work begins and reviewed as conditions change.

  • Quality Assurance

    02

    Quality requirements are defined up front — materials, methods, inspection points and acceptance criteria — so that expectations are clear to everyone involved.

  • Quality Control

    03

    Inspection and testing are carried out at defined stages, with records retained so that completed work can be verified rather than assumed.

  • Risk Management

    04

    Risk assessments, method statements and permit requirements are prepared for the work at hand, with controls reviewed before and during execution.

  • Professional Standards

    05

    We work to recognised industry practice, follow project specifications and coordinate openly with clients, consultants and other trades.

Working principle

No activity starts without a method statement, a risk assessment and the access required to do it correctly. Inspection points are agreed before work is covered up.
